subject: Next steps: choosing hosting path for SmartRetail quickstart
messages:
From: Claire Park <claire@smartretail.io>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 15 May 2028 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Quick follow-up on hosting path after demo — pilot constraints

Thanks again for the demo this morning — the team found the latency and batching examples helpful. A couple items we want to confirm before we finalize the pilot scope: 

1) Data and hosting: we are comfortable with Redwood's hosted API for initial evaluation, but we have two principal constraints: data residency for PII / cardholder metadata (we can share a sanitized sample) and an internal procurement requirement that persistent logs be retained for 90 days. Does hosted support that, or would we need Dedicated / Private?

2) Traffic footprint: our prototype will generate spiky traffic — roughly 20 TPS for short bursts (30–60s) during peak business hours and average 1–2 TPS otherwise. Token sizes will be ~200 tokens per request. Is hosted API able to handle the burst profile without pre-provisioning? What are default rate limits and how do we request higher burst caps for a short pilot?

3) Quickstart ask: can you share a one-page checklist of the steps to get sandbox endpoints, recommended endpoints (chat vs text-gen), and how to enable prefix/KV caching for our use-case?

I've attached a short priorities doc. Tom L. (procurement) is on cc to flag any contract concerns early.

Thanks — Claire

Attachments:
- SmartRetail_Pilot_Priorities.pdf (summary of pilot goals, data notes)
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Claire Park <claire@smartretail.io>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, Tom Lambert <tom.lambert@smartretail.io>
Date: Tue, 15 May 2028 12:35:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quick follow-up on hosting path after demo — pilot constraints

Claire — great to hear the demo landed. Quick recap and proposed next steps below.

Short answers up front:
- Hosted API: suitable for most pilots; supports audit logs and 90-day retention via our standard logging + export (we can push to a customer bucket or include in contract).
- Burst traffic: hosted can absorb short bursts via autoscaling; default per-account rate limits are conservative for safety but we can increase burst caps for the pilot after we collect a short traffic profile.
- Quickstart checklist: attaching our one-sheet (redwood-quickstart-checklist.xlsx) with sandbox endpoint steps and recommended endpoint mappings.

Actionable plan (proposed):
1) You: confirm a sanitized sample traffic trace (5–10 minutes) and which fields are PII so we can validate retention path.
2) We (Redwood): provision a sandbox hosted endpoint with the following defaults for the pilot (can change after profiling):
   - endpoint: /v1/hosts/smartretail-chat (chat-style) and /v1/hosts/smartretail-gen (text-gen fallback)
   - default rate limits: 60 requests/minute per API key; burst to 120 req/min for short windows with autoscale (we can raise this for pilot to 300 req/min on request)
   - recommended batching: continuous batching with 50ms latency target; enable prefix KV caching for repeated prompts
3) Procurement: Aditya will share a short SOW and sandbox access order form.
4) Next call: 30-minute ops call to finalize token-estimates and confirm retention/export path — proposed Thu 17 May.

Notes / constraints:
- If SmartRetail requires an SLA-backed 99.9% latency SLA or sustained >400 req/s for production, Dedicated or Private would be a better long-term option; for evaluation and quick feedback, Hosted is faster to stand up.
- For PII/logging: hosted supports customer-managed export; Private (VPC) is recommended if you need full on-prem data isolation.

I attached the quickstart checklist and the pilot priorities you sent (file names below). If Tom or procurement need a contract redline template for a data-retention clause, I can loop in our legal ops.

Proposed meeting times (PT): Thu 17 May 10:00 or 14:00 — does either work?

Best,
Hannah

Subject: Re: Quick follow-up on hosting path after demo — pilot constraints

Claire / Hannah — adding a brief commercial note so procurement has context.

Pricing / provisioning notes:
- Hosted pilot: billed usage + temporary increased burst caps for the pilot month. We can add a short pilot credit if you want to run higher burst windows for the first 30 days (I’ve penciled a modest credit in HS-43218).
- Dedicated: recommended when sustained throughput > 300–400 req/s or when you need guaranteed per-token unit economics. Typical lead time for dedicated pools is 4–6 weeks for provisioning.
- Private (VPC/on-prem): used when contractual data residency or audit constraints cannot be satisfied by hosted export options. Longer lead time and additional license/engagement fees.

If you can confirm the expected 95th-percentile sustained requests and peak burst window (start/end time cadence), I’ll prepare two quick pricing sketches: Hosted pilot and Dedicated baseline.

Next steps from my side: I’ll prepare a short mutual action plan that maps Responsible/Owner and due dates (MVP pilot sandbox -> ops call -> pilot launch -> review). Hannah — can you confirm whether the proposed Thu 17 May 10:00 PT works for an ops call?

Thanks,
Aditya Rao
